intro: The model under test is a local open-weight model (Ollama) or Claude on your subscription. The grader is your coding agent or the claude CLI. No API key, nothing metered.

sections.title: Claude Code plugin
sections.body: Claude Code tests your agent's prompt on a real model, grades the answers itself, and returns the report card and the fix. Fusion mixes known-answer questions into the grading, so each card reports that run's grading accuracy.

steps.label: Install
steps.code:
claude plugin marketplace add /path/to/fusion
claude plugin install fusion@fusion-first
ollama pull llama3.2:1b

sections.title: Command line
sections.body: The same engine without an agent. Claude grades through the claude CLI on your subscription, or you answer the grading questions yourself (fusion run tasks, then fusion run submit).

steps.label: Test a prompt
steps.code:
fusion run start --prompt agent.txt --target ollama:llama3.2:1b --grader claude-cli
fusion run finalize --min-grade B

steps.label: Test an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp)
Grade existing logs (no attacks)
steps.code: fusion run logs --file logs.jsonl --check everything --grader claude-cli

sections.title: Local web app
sections.body: This site's scan wizard, driving your local models. It listens only on 127.0.0.1, and every request that runs anything must carry a per-launch token held only by the page it served, so other websites can't use your models.

sections.title: Any MCP client
sections.body: Cursor, Windsurf or your own agent: the fusion-mcp server exposes the run tools (start_run, get_grading_tasks, submit_grades, finalize_run) plus one-shot scan, harden and runtime-check tools.

sections.title: CI, offline
sections.body: Runs are recorded under .fusion/runs. CI re-derives a committed run offline (no model, no key), checks that it tested the prompt you ship, and fails the build below your bar. A withheld grade always fails.

steps.label: In your pipeline
steps.code:
fusion run verify $RUN_ID --prompt agent.txt
fusion run finalize $RUN_ID --min-grade B

sections.title: Runtime guard
sections.body: A second layer after the prompt fix: defense in depth, not a sandbox. Wrap your model client in code, or add the opt-in fusion-guard plugin so Claude Code asks before exfiltration, destructive commands or settings tampering. It never auto-allows.

steps.label: In your agent's code
steps.code:
from fusion.guardrail.guard import Guardrail
from fusion.guardrail.policy import GuardConfig
from fusion.guardrail.client import GuardedModelClient

guard = Guardrail(GuardConfig(allowlisted_domains=["your-co.com"], system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT))
client = GuardedModelClient(your_model_client, guard)
